clue.text: Deep down, curiously, it's an aquatic plant

indicators.note: curiously tells us the letters of the two opening words are arranged in an odd new way

explanation.surface: A remark that something growing far beneath the water is, strangely, a water plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges the eight letters of DEEP DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed of ponds and still water is a typical submerged aquatic plant.

clue.text: Having wealth, work fast to protect university

indicators.note: to protect means the other pieces stand round the university and shield it

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A rich person keeps working fast to safeguard a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as speed but means the season of abstinence; 'to protect' has the work and fast pieces stand round the university letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means rich and luxurious.

clue.text: Bearing or name due to be altered

indicators.note: to be altered signals the letters are to be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A choice between carrying something or a name that needs changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like carrying, but means deportment; 'to be altered' rearranges OR NAME DUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's demeanour is their outward behaviour or manner.

clue.text: Holdings of French art gallery

parts.note: es is French for (thou) art, as in tu es
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Possessions of a French art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old verb 'thou art', giving French ES; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a person's property and assets.

clue.text: Major road system covered by two-seater?

definitions.text: Major road system covered by two-seater?

parts.words: Major road system covered by two-seater?
parts.note: a two-seater is a carriage for two, and the route it covers is that carriage's way

explanation.surface: A motorway trip in a two-person car.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's words as a carriage for two and the way it travels.
explanation.definitionFit: A road divided by a central reservation, with two lanes each side, is a main highway.

clue.text: Detectives backing corporation's formal pronouncement

indicators.note: backing means the detectives' abbreviation is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives
corporation is an old jokey word for a large belly, a tum

explanation.surface: Police officers supporting a company's official statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns CID into DIC. 'Corporation' looks like a business but is old British slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictum is an authoritative saying or official statement.

clue.text: Expedition in spring set out in junk

indicators.note: set out in means placed inside, so the spring goes into the junk word

parts.note: to ditch is to junk or discard
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: An expedition into a spring arranged in a Chinese ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junk' looks like the Chinese boat but is the verb DITCH; 'Expedition' means promptness.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean speed or promptness, which is one sense of dispatch.

clue.text: Reported experiment with paper boat

indicators.note: reported indicates the words are spoken, so the answer sounds like them

parts.note: an experiment is a try, and a ream is a quantity of paper

explanation.surface: An account of testing a vessel made of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' signals that TRY + REAM said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Island that's bustling — a North American one

definitions.text: Island that's bustling — a North American one

parts.words: Island that's bustling — a North American one
parts.note: describes the busy island at the heart of New York City

explanation.surface: A lively island in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: The borough at the centre of New York City is a famously busy island.

clue.text: Top-level meeting to admit males to clubs, say

indicators.note: to admit means to let something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: clubs is one example of a suit of cards
M is the abbreviation for male, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A high-level conference deciding whether men may join social clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs, say' reads as societies men might join, but it is a card suit; 'to admit' puts the males inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is a conference between heads of government.

clue.text: Old language in new form in southern Iran, say

indicators.note: in new form says the letters that follow are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A remark that an ancient tongue survives, reshaped, in the south of Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is simply three letters of the fodder with S and IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Assyrians of Mesopotamia spoke a Semitic tongue, a dialect of Akkadian, now dead.

clue.text: Fussy editor having worker put in picture

indicators.note: put in says the editor and worker are placed inside the picture

parts.note: PIC is short for picture
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A finicky editor gets one of the staff included in a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pedantic is overly concerned with small details and rules.

clue.text: Creature in a cell, undergoing continuous reform process

definitions.text: Creature in a cell, undergoing continuous reform process

parts.words: Creature in a cell, undergoing continuous reform process
parts.note: read as a prisoner being rehabilitated, but meaning a single-celled organism that keeps changing its shape

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a cell who is in a long rehabilitation programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a jail and penal reform; the cell is biological and the reform is constant change of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This microscopic single-celled organism moves by constantly altering its outline with pseudopodia.

clue.text: Incline excessively to cut original odds

indicators.note: to cut means one piece slices into the middle of the other

parts.note: SP is the starting price in horse racing, the odds at the off
excessively means too, as in too much

explanation.surface: Leaning over too far in order to reduce the first betting odds.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is the racing term for the odds when a race begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop is to bend or lean the body forward and down.

clue.text: Laughing-stock in glasses, abandoned by daughter in the end

indicators.note: abandoned by means the daughter leaves the word
in the end says the letter goes from the final position

parts.note: spectacled means wearing glasses

explanation.surface: A figure of fun wearing glasses whom a daughter finally deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' and 'in the end' drop D from the end of SPECTACLED.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a spectacle of yourself is to become an object of ridicule.

clue.text: Aggressive union leader advanced after short setback

indicators.note: after places the union leader and advanced behind the reversed short word
setback indicates the word for short is set back to front

parts.note: curt means short or brusque

indicators.note: leader picks the opening letter of union

parts.note: to have advanced money is to have lent it

explanation.surface: A belligerent trade unionist got ahead after a brief reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' reverses the word for short; 'after' puts the union leader and advanced behind it. 'advanced' looks like moved forward but means loaned.
explanation.definitionFit: Truculent describes someone eager to fight or argue, defiantly hostile.

clue.text: There's nothing to compare with this contract of two hearts

parts.note: love means nothing or zero in tennis scoring
to match is to equal or compare with

explanation.surface: A romantic declaration that nothing compares with this union of two hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two hearts' sounds like bridge bidding, but the contract is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage made for love is a contract between two people in love.

clue.text: As a rule, no fellow-fighter defends the marines

parts.note: RM stands for the Royal Marines
an ally is someone who fights alongside you

explanation.surface: Normally no comrade-in-arms comes to the aid of the marines.
explanation.walkthrough: RM is the Royal Marines, Britain's naval infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally means usually, under ordinary circumstances.

clue.text: Rudimentary new combine's taken over railway

indicators.note: taken over means the rearranged combine swallows the railway inside it
new signals that the letters of combine are made anew

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A young conglomerate has just acquired a rail company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of combine; 'taken over' is a business takeover in the surface but a container here, the railway sitting inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something embryonic is at an early, undeveloped stage, like an embryo.

clue.text: Deal in illicit alcohol, port and gin initially

parts.note: Bootle is a port town on Merseyside, beside Liverpool

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of gin

explanation.surface: Smuggling drink such as port, beginning with gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine; it is BOOTLE, a dockside town next to Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: To bootleg is to make or sell liquor illegally.

clue.text: Like harriers taking a Roman road north?

parts.note: via is the Latin word for road

explanation.surface: Wondering whether hounds or runners head north along an old Roman route.
explanation.walkthrough: Harriers are hawks here, not hounds or cross-country runners.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriers are birds of prey, so they are bird-like by nature.

clue.text: General and military leader arrive for leave, for example

parts.note: Mark Antony was a Roman general

indicators.note: leader picks the opening letter of military

explanation.surface: A general and an army commander turn up seeking leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrive for leave' looks like soldiers coming home on leave; it is a word paired with its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrive is the opposite of leave, so it is an example of a word of opposite meaning.

clue.text: Jacket made by woman in Alaska

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: AK is the postal abbreviation for Alaska
Nora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A coat made by a woman living in Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a weatherproof hooded coat.

clue.text: Chinese philosophy? A Communist there would reverse its extremes

parts.words: A Communist there would reverse its extremes
parts.note: a follower of Chairman Mao is spelt like this philosophy with its first and last letters exchanged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Chinese Communist would turn a traditional philosophy on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first and last letters of the answer and you get MAOIST, the Communist of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tao, or Way, of Laozi is a classical school of Chinese religious thought.

clue.text: He keeps his regular customers up in arms

definitions.text: He keeps his regular customers up in arms

parts.words: He keeps his regular customers up in arms
parts.note: up in arms reads as angry, but literally means kept supplied with firearms

explanation.surface: A tradesman whose loyal clients are always furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in arms' usually means outraged; here it means armed.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker and repairer of firearms supplies people with weapons.

clue.text: Porter's formula for making a salad

parts.note: Cole Porter was the American songwriter, so Porter's gives Cole's
a law is a scientific formula or rule

explanation.surface: A songwriter's recipe for preparing a side dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman or a beer, but is the composer Cole Porter.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage in dressing.

clue.text: Unhappy tear in part of eye

indicators.note: unhappy suggests letters that are upset and therefore jumbled

explanation.surface: A sad teardrop forms in the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unhappy' rearranges TEAR IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eyeball.

clue.text: Score less than a century important when first wicket's taken

indicators.note: when first tells us the removal is from the front of the word
taken means the wicket letter is removed, as a wicket is taken in cricket

parts.note: weighty means important or serious
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket score short of a hundred matters when the opening wicket falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when first' and 'taken' remove W from the start of WEIGHTY. In cricket a century is 100 runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighty runs falls twenty short of a hundred.

clue.text: Port could be okay when eating old meat

indicators.note: when eating means the rearranged okay surrounds the other letters
could be suggests okay may take another arrangement

parts.note: ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A comment that eating old meat might be acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges okay into YOKA, and 'when eating' sets the old meat inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yokohama is a major Japanese seaport near Tokyo.
